name: bytecode_interpreter
spec: Create a bytecode interpreter for a simple programming language in Python using only the standard library. The system has three stages: a lexer that tokenizes source code, a compiler that produces bytecode instructions, and a virtual machine that executes the bytecode. The language should support variables, arithmetic, conditionals, loops, functions, and print output.
features: A lexer tokenizes source code into tokens (numbers, identifiers, operators, keywords, delimiters)
The lexer handles integer and float literals, string literals, and single-line comments
A compiler parses tokens and emits a sequence of bytecode instructions
The language supports variable assignment and retrieval (e.g. x = 10)
The language supports arithmetic expressions with correct operator precedence (+, -, *, /, parentheses)
The language supports comparison operators (==, !=, <, >, <=, >=) producing boolean results
The language supports if/else conditional blocks
The language supports function definitions with parameters and return values
The language supports function calls with arguments
A built-in print statement outputs values to stdout
The virtual machine executes bytecode using a stack-based architecture
Meaningful error messages are produced for syntax errors with line numbers
Meaningful error messages are produced for runtime errors (division by zero, undefined variables)
The interpreter accepts a source file path as a command-line argument and executes it
At least 3 example programs are included that demonstrate all language features
